films.name: Yo (Love Is a Rebellious Bird)
films.short_description: Anna spends a decade obsessively building a detailed 1/3-scale version of her friend’s house after losing her. It’s just big enough for Anna to squeeze through the door, and inside lives a puppet of her friend Yo.
films.description:
Anna spends a decade obsessively building a detailed 1/3-scale version of her friend's house after losing her. It’s just big enough for Anna to squeeze through the door. Inside lives a puppet of her friend Yo. When the pair met, Yo was 73 and Anna just 24. Over the decades, they form a deep bond. After Yo's death, Anna re-constructs a magical space where Yo's stories unfold, and their relationship continues.


The film juxtaposes intimate vérité of Yo's last year with Anna's creative interpretations of Yo's dramatic life stories. Born in Switzerland in 1924, Yo lived life on her own terms, defying expectations around sexuality, mothering, aging, and even death. As the film blurs memory, time and invention, it also reveals the power of artistic creation to channel -and share- grief and love.

films.name: Glorious Summer
films.short_description: A sun-drenched Renaissance palace. Three women remain in a carefree state of limbo, tended to by an unseen, all-providing system. But as cracks in the paradise begin to appear, they are faced with a life-altering choice: escape or remain in the perfect illusion?
films.description:
A sun-drenched Renaissance palace. Three women exist in an airy state of suspension, a liminal, responsibility-free bubble, where summer never ends. An enigmatic system fulfills all their needs - providing food, entertainment and a daily routine focused on wellness affirmations. There’s just one rule: they are forbidden to cross the surrounding wall.


Soon, cracks begin to appear in this idyllic picture: using a ‘touch language’ - as some things can't be said out loud, secretly practicing how to die, which is supposed to be their ticket to ‘another place’. Long-suppressed anger and a desperate need to escape emerge. Will the girls, raised in a state of perpetual immaturity, manage to break free from the boundaries enforced by the system?

films.name: Run Amok
films.short_description: A teenage girl decides to stage a full, musical reenactment of the shooting that took place at her high school 10 years ago.
films.description:
Meg Littleton, amateur harpist and professional teacher’s pet, lives with her aunt, uncle and perennially popular cousin, Penny. When Meg discovers a commemoration ceremony is being planned for the shooting that took place at her high school ten years ago, she knows she must contribute something.


After all, the shooting claimed the lives of three students, and one teacher— Meg’s mom. Meg decides to stage a full, musical reenactment of the event, and convinces Penny to star in the show. With her cast of high school misfits, Meg attempts to pull off this bizarre, tender, and unwieldy undertaking— while the adults, armed with denial, dogma, and rubber bullet guns, do everything they can to stop her.

films.name: Crystal Cross
films.short_description: A quirky Christian singer and a suicidal dad drive cross-country, forging an unlikely bond through bad decisions, bizarre roadside attractions, and an all-original soundtrack. "Crystal Cross" is a hilarious, bittersweet road trip about two lost souls finding comfort (but not salvation) in each other’s messes.
films.description:
Crystal Cross is the story of two unlikely companions on a doomed but beautiful road trip across America. Dotty, a Christian singer in trouble, believes she’s received a sign from God when she meets James, a man who looks strikingly like Jesus. For Dotty, James is her ride out of town and a chance to reverse her fate. For James, however, the journey has a darker purpose. Broken by the loss of his daughter and after several failed suicide attempts, he is driving cross-country to California to finally end his life.


What follows is an odd-couple love story — not quite a romance, but a connection that grows out of desperation, humor, music, and the long miles between them. Dotty clings to her dreams of stardom while hiding a secret that could destroy them both. James, a father without a child and a musician who no longer plays, resists every effort to be saved. As they travel, their bond deepens in strange, contradictory ways: moments of beauty at roadside attractions, recording booths, desert blooms, and drunken spirals reveal both their flaws and their fragile hope.


Crystal Cross explores the absurdity and tenderness of survival, faith, and failure in modern America. It is both a darkly comic odyssey and a meditation on love in its rawest form — love that doesn’t fix or promise, but simply keeps you alive for one more mile.

films.name: Uncommitted
films.short_description: Uncommitted follows Arab and Muslim American organizers who transform grief over Gaza into a grassroots movement that galvanizes nearly a million protest votes during the 2024 Democratic presidential primaries. From Dearborn to the Democratic National Convention, the film chronicles an emerging political coalition as it discovers its collective power and tests the possibilities, and limits, of representation, dissent, and American democracy.
films.description:
Uncommitted follows Arab and Muslim American organizers Lexi Zeidan, Layla Elabed, and Abbas Alawieh as they transform grief over Gaza into an unprecedented grassroots political movement. Beginning in Dearborn, Michigan, their campaign galvanizes nearly a million protest votes during the 2024 Democratic presidential primaries, challenging party leaders to support a ceasefire and demonstrating that their communities’ votes must be earned rather than assumed.


The movement carries its demands to the Democratic National Convention in Chicago, where even a request for a Palestinian American speaker is ultimately rejected. With intimate vérité access, Uncommitted focuses not on Palestinian suffering itself, but on what communities do in response, building coalitions, exercising political leverage, and challenging the institutions that claim to represent them.


More than an election documentary, Uncommitted captures the emergence of a new political coalition and a movement whose impact continues to reshape conversations about Palestine, representation, and political power in America.

films.name: A Woman's Work
films.short_description: A young woman in rural Kentucky works as a coal miner to provide for her two younger sisters after losing her parents; her father, who was also a coal miner, to the opioid epidemic.
films.description: Jolene has taken up a job in the coal mines in rural Kentucky - a job her father did before he died. She has to remain in the closet due to the place where she lives - while nothing is illegal, it is still frowned upon - and she accepts that there are certain sides of herself that she must keep hidden. Jolene constantly sacrifices for others; her love has to be hidden from prejudiced eyes, she works as a coal miner in order to keep a roof over her family's head and food on the table, and it rests upon her shoulders to care for her younger sisters even though she’s still figuring out how to care for herself.

films.short_description: Fighting More Than Fire is a documentary that captures the living history of Black firefighters in Tulsa, OK.
films.description: Fighting More Than Fire is a documentary that explores the untold history of Black firefighters in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Through personal stories, first-hand accounts, and following a “day-in-the-life” of these heroes, the film captures the struggles and triumphs of the men who broke barriers in a segregated fire department. This film preserves their legacy and honors the generations who paved the way for today’s firefighters.

films.name: Wood Street
films.short_description: Two unhoused men turned community leaders— John and LaMonté —organize their neighbors in the face of displacement, addiction, and a failing social system.
films.description: WOOD STREET follows a year in the life of Oakland’s largest unhoused encampment as its residents face an imminent eviction that threatens to dismantle their community. As notices appear and police move in, residents organize — building barricades, filing lawsuits, and protesting at City Hall to fight for their right to stay. Told through immersive verité, the film places viewers inside the encampment, capturing the urgency, resilience, and emotional toll of collective resistance. At its center are John and LaMonté, whose bond is tested as pressure mounts — LaMonté’s mental health deteriorates while John struggles to remain sober. When the eviction comes, the community is physically erased, but its spirit endures.

films.name: All American Girls
films.short_description: All American Girls explores inclusivity in U.S. historical narratives through the famed American Girl brand, which was brought to life by legendary entrepreneur, Pleasant Rowland.
films.description: All American Girls pulls back the curtain, revealing the inner world of American Girl; the wildly popular brand that shaped girlhood for generations from the '80s onward. Today, the brand is a cultural touchstone, triggering debates about social and political issues. American Girl was founded by Midwestern schoolteacher Pleasant Rowland, who is sharing her story for the first time after evading the spotlight for decades.

films.short_description: What begins as a nostalgic road trip for two estranged friends quickly spirals out of control when they discover they've been unwittingly transporting drugs, forcing old tensions in their relationship to bubble to the surface.

films.name: Landscapes of Memory
films.short_description: LANDSCAPES OF MEMORY follows Leah Galant’s journey through Germany as she reckons with family trauma and the weight of historical memory of the Holocaust. Interwoven stories of a Holocaust-survivor descendant, a Nazi-descendant historian, exiled Palestinian artists, and her father’s ALS, reveal the uses and abuses of memory culture.
films.description:
When director Leah Galant left the U.S. for Berlin in 2021, she thought she was going on a traditional “third-generation return” to uncover her family’s Holocaust history. But, after being detained while filming a pro-Palestine demonstration, and charged with antisemitism, she quickly realized that confronting inherited trauma meant grappling with the present, not just the past.


From brass “Stolpersteine” (stumbling stones) marking former Jewish homes, to concrete slabs, reminders of the Nazi regime’s atrocities are built into the German landscape. Yet cracks appear in those memorials. The rise of far-right extremism both in the streets and at the ballot box raises urgent questions about what lessons, if any, have truly been learned. Holocaust memory is often rigidly policed, Palestine activism is equated with antisemitism, and Arab and Muslim communities are increasingly surveilled and silenced.


LANDSCAPES OF MEMORY is a documentary weaving personal essay, observational storytelling, and intimate character studies to explore the uses and abuses of Holocaust memory. Filmed in the years before and months after the seismic shift of October 7th, the film follows three main protagonists: a third-generation Holocaust survivor’s descendant, Eli, a third-generation Nazi descendant, Johannes, and a Palestinian artist, Michael, each trying to understand what memory means in the present.


This journey through memorials past, present and future follows director Leah Galant’s personal exploration of history, memory and trauma. As her father’s health, and his ability to speak and share family histories, deteriorates from ALS, she takes on new responsibilities to carry her family's story of their Holocaust survival. Through voice notes, as he increasingly relies on text-to-speech, the film interweaves intimate yet universal explorations on the burden of history, and what it means to learn from the past to shape the present.

films.short_description: In the wake of a terrifying encounter, an overwhelmed drag queen struggles under the weight of public attention.

films.short_description: After the arrival of a nun with mystical visions, Sister Miriam becomes envious of her rival's sudden notoriety and begins falsifying miracles in a grotesque game of spiritual cat-and-mouse.

films.name: something still
films.short_description: When a heartbroken man returns to his ex-boyfriends' apartment, they're forced to confront the aftermath of a boundary they chose to blur.
films.description:
Tom (John Brodsky), a young queer man, returns to the apartment he once shared with his ex-boyfriend, Max (Zane Phillips), to pack up his belongings. Entering the space triggers memories of their passionate beginnings—their electric chemistry and surprising tenderness—now a stark contrast to Max’s cold, distant demeanor. As Tom navigates the echoes of their past, he reflects on a pivotal decision: inviting Dan (Panagiotis Margetis), a charming stranger from Grindr, into their relationship for a casual fling.


What started as playful experimentation spiraled into an unexpected bond between Max and Dan, leaving Tom sidelined and heartbroken. Now, standing among the remnants of their life together, Tom must confront the choices that led to the relationship's unraveling and find a way to move forward.

films.name: Matches
films.short_description: After matching with a famous actor on a dating app, Ryan is invited to a party at his mansion where he is unexpectedly thrown into a cut throat competition for the actor’s heart.
films.description: After Ryan, a hopeless romantic, matches with Hollywood heartthrob Sam Ellis on a dating app, he receives an invitation to an exclusive party at Sam's mansion. Ryan's dreams of romance become a nightmare as he realizes everyone at the party has also matched with Sam on a dating app, and he’s been thrust into a cutthroat competition for the actor's heart.

films.name: Las Cosas Que Brillan
films.short_description: A curious trans mermaid defies her mother’s warnings to venture up to the surface, only to discover the world above is not what she dreamt.
films.description: A curious trans mermaid defies her mother’s warnings to venture up to the surface, only to discover the world above is not what she dreamt. Las Cosas Que Brillan explores the impacts of environmental destruction, and the danger of being desired in a postcolonial world.

films.name: Is it Like, a Date?!?
films.short_description: Two teenage girls at an art museum are desperate to figure out if their meetup is a date — while their parents connect in the parking lot and wind up on a date of their own.
films.description: Two teenage girls at an art museum are desperate to figure out if their meetup is a date — while their parents connect in the parking lot and wind up on a date of their own. Stylistically, this lighthearted romantic comedy jumps between the conventions of lush period romances and the approachable style of modern romantic comedies, contrasting the girls' young love and their parent's casual courtship. Is it, Like, a Date?!? explores a universal story about the spark of connection through a joyful queer lens that spotlights proud parents of color.

films.name: Sam Wants Her Sweater Back
films.short_description: Three queer friends launch a half-witted heist to steal back a sweater from one of their exes. But recovering from heartbreak isn't quite the slick-lit, neon-noir adventure one of them imagines.
films.description:
Andi and Max’s best friend Sam was dumped months ago. But Sam’s ex, Poppy, still hasn’t

returned her sweater. THE Sweater. Andi, recently dumped herself (but why even bring that up?), won’t stand for it!


So, in Andi’s mind the world becomes a gritty, neon laced action-thriller as the three infiltrate Poppy’s house party in search of The Sweater. As the night unfolds and multiple plans unravel it becomes clear Andi’s vehemence has little to do with her friend’s knitwear and all to do with hiding from her own heartbreak.


A delightful romp from denial to acceptance after being broken up with, SAM WANTS HER SWEATER BACK is a queer/trans, buddy-heist joyride about recovery from heartbreak with the love of friends and community.

films.name: This is Not a Heartbeat
films.short_description: An essayistic exploration of ultrasound technology and the spectre of the fetal heartbeat in American politics, THIS IS NOT A HEARTBEAT asks: when machines mediate how we see the body, what are we actually seeing, and who gets to decide what it means?
films.description:
THIS IS NOT A HEARTBEAT interrogates how science is translated, mythologized, and weaponized through the story of one misunderstood sound: the fetal heartbeat. At six weeks, the so-called ‘heartbeat’ is not the sound of a heart at all, but machine-generated audio. Yet this manufactured signal has become deeply emotional and politically charged, used to restrict abortion access across the U.S.


Blending poetic voiceover, archival footage, and experimental sound design, the film examines how ultrasound technology doesn’t just capture reality, it constructs it. The film asks: when machines mediate our view of the body, what are we really seeing, and who decides what it means?

films.name: Born Secret
films.short_description: A filmmaker returns to his home town that built the atomic bomb.
films.description: A filmmaker returns to his hometown, Oak Ridge, TN, the secret city that built the atomic bomb. There, he meets the workers who created humanity's greatest weapon that now wrestle with their legacy, while their grandchildren inherit a world on the brink of nuclear catastrophe.

films.name: Greensburg Anew
films.short_description: Spanning more than three decades, a photographer returns to Greensburg, Kansas, tracing its journey from life before an EF5 tornado to a sustainable future, while asking what it means to live with the knowledge that disaster could strike again.
films.description: In 1993, Susanne Walström photographed everyday life in Greensburg, Kansas. Fourteen years later, an EF5 tornado devastated the town, destroying 95% of its buildings and forever changing the lives of those who remained. Years later, she returns with her photographs to explore how the disaster has shaped the community and how Greensburg has reinvented itself as a model for sustainable living. But what does it mean to build a future in a place where tornado shelters are part of everyday life and the possibility of another disaster is never far away? Greensburg Anew is a portrait of resilience, vulnerability, and a community living with the memory of what happened and the knowledge that it could happen again.

films.name: HER BABY DIDN'T BLOCK HER JUMPSHOT
films.short_description: Before Title IX, Iowa high school girls thrilled fans playing 6-on-6 basketball. When All-State star Jane Christoffer was banned for becoming a mother, she challenged the their notion of farm-girl femininity, demanding her right to play ball.
films.description: For most of the 20th century, Iowa high school girls thrilled fans in packed stadiums playing 6-on-6 basketball. Empowered as athletes, they transformed the sport into the Midwest’s biggest spectacle. When sophomore All-State forward Jane Christoffer became a mother and was cast out of the league, she challenged their notion of farm-girl femininity, demanding her right to play ball.

films.name: Brimstone Terrace
films.short_description: When a depressed public defender ends his own life, he is sentenced to an eternity in Hell. However, after Satan takes notice of his skills, he is offered an afterlife-changing deal that may not fall in line with his own values.

films.name: AMAZING LIVE SEA MONKEYS
films.short_description: From her crumbling estate on the Potomac, Yolanda Signorelli is engaged in a battle to wrest control of her late husband Harold’s iconic toy Amazing Live Sea-Monkeys back from the corporate men who she insists stole them from her, and to rescue them from the stain of her husband’s dark legacy.
films.description: From her crumbling estate on the Potomac, Yolanda Signorelli is engaged in a David-and-Goliath battle to wrest control of her late husband Harold’s iconic toy Amazing Live Sea-Monkeys back from the corporate men who she insists stole them from her. Harold von Braunhut and Yolanda Signorelli had worked together for forty years before Harold - a genius magician, scientist and inventor – passed away and left his iconic novelty toy in Yolanda’s care. With an explosive reveal, AMAZING LIVE SEA MONKEYS dives into the depths of the American psyche, as von Braunhut harbored a dark secret. Yolanda alone possesses the true Sea-Monkeys formula and she alone must free them, not only from their captors, but also from the stain of her husband’s tarnished legacy.

films.name: The Peril at Pincer Point
films.short_description: On a quest to prove his competency, an inept sound recordist finds himself entangled in a nautical prophecy on the spectral island of Pincer Point.
films.description:
Jim Baitte, a layabout sound designer desperate to prove himself, is working on a new horror flick from the tyrannical yet lauded b-movie director P.W. Griffin. Accused of lacking vision and creative courage, Jim is sent to the remote island where the film was shot to capture a sound powerful enough to elevate the film's finale.


Once there, eerie local fables surface: for years, ambitious and headstrong youth have lost their souls to a ghostly sea captain for his spectral crew. As Jim entangles himself further into the bizarre locals, scenery, and prophecy, he can’t help but ponder the ever-confirming legend, and if recording it might just cost him more than his career.

films.name: 8 Seconds at the Three Sisters
films.short_description: A filmmaker’s solo canoe trip to an ancient bald cypress swamp takes an unexpected turn, prompting him to reconstruct an experience whose images and sounds were lost to the river.
films.description: A filmmaker canoes up North Carolina’s Black River to the Three Sisters Swamp, chasing light through ancient bald cypress groves. What begins as a familiar act of observation and recording takes an uncanny turn. Using past footage and sound, the film reconstructs what was seen, what was heard—and what cannot be explained.

films.name: Crumble
films.short_description: Crumble is an experimental short film about identity, trauma, loss, and the search for healing. A woman drifts between dream and reality, feeling alone and unseen in her own life. When she meets the child she once was, she begins to understand that healing is not something given by others. It starts when she has the courage to face herself.
films.description:
CRUMBLE follows a young woman through dreams, memories and fragments of her past. She carries experiences from her childhood that are still with her as an adult. She feels unseen and disconnected from the world around her, almost like a ghost in her own life.


In her dreams, these feelings take different forms. Her teeth crumble, parts of her body disappear and she is chased. The dreams bring back fears, loss and things from the past that never really left her.


As she moves through these images, she eventually comes face to face with the child she once was. In that moment, she begins to see herself differently and understands that facing herself might be the first step towards healing.

films.name: Hungerstruck
films.short_description: When an influencer starved for fame finds the role of a Cannibal killer, she documents her audition process through vlogs, determined to prove to her loyal audience she'll go as far and as method as possible to keep them watching.
films.description: Victoria is an influencer who desperately wants to be famous. She works at a local butcher shop and documents her vegetarian LA lifestyle to her devoted fans, or as she calls them, “Victorians.” One day, she finds an audition for the role of a cannibal, and she decides to vlog her audition process to her audience. In desperate need of getting the role (and new subscribers), she goes full-on method and tries “meat” for the first time. Despite her newfound hunger, she soon discovers the movie business is just as exploitative as the internet, women are just pieces of meat to consume. And you can only go so far to please your audience before it starts eating away at you…

films.name: The Big Grate
films.short_description: The quiet ritual of preparing the pre-Columbian soup pozole unravels into a visceral reflection on cultural identity, memory, and violence in this reimagined take on Martin Scorsese’s early-career film, The Big Shave.
films.description: What would a 2025 version of Scorsese’s The Big Shave look like today? The Big Grate is an experimental body-horror allegory using cryptic imagery to examine colonialism’s impact on identity, food politics, and supply chains, and how its scars persist in what we eat, how we live, and who we become.

films.name: The Last Bateau
films.short_description: Almost a half century after her great-grandfather’s voice was captured on cassette tapes, a woman returns to Caddo Lake to restore the last boat he built and listen to the legacy he left behind.
films.description: In the quiet woods of East Texas, producer Brittani Mathis uncovers a wooden bateau built by her great-grandfather, Wyatt Moore, and a box of cassette tapes where his voice still lingers. Nearly fifty years after he recorded them, she returns to Caddo Lake to restore the last bateau he built. In doing so, she reconnects with the craft, memory, and lineage that shaped then both. Anchored around archival audio and quiet observation, this lyrical documentary moves like memory.

films.name: The Phenomenal Nothing
films.short_description: Two women in mirrored routines find within the rhythm of repetition a moment of unspoken connection.
films.description:
The Phenomenal Nothing explores the unlikely connection between two women on seemingly opposite life paths. The film is a meditation on time,

its repetition, its rhythm, and its quiet grip on our daily lives. Is time linear, or are we simply moving through endless cycles? Rinse and repeat. Rinse

and repeat.


One woman folds paper; the other folds towels. These mirrored gestures, mundane yet meditative, highlight the subtle ways our lives can echo one another. Through repetition, routine begins to blur individuality. Yet, within that blurring lies the possibility of something more: recognition, connection, and perhaps transcendence.

films.name: When We Were Live
films.short_description: Told entirely through restored public access footage, When We Were Live revives the unforgettable characters who turned an Austin community TV station into a world-famous stage for self-expression.
films.description:
Long before YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram, public access was the original platform for unfiltered creativity and community connection — a precursor to today’s social media, where ordinary people could broadcast themselves to their community.


Made up almost entirely of restored public access footage shot by Austinites over the last 50 years, each clip is a standalone story that reveals the city’s spirit from a new point of view. Among the film’s many characters are Livia, a PhD student turned late-night host whose uncensored sex-and-relationships call-in show became a cult favorite; Carmen Banana, a jovial drag queen whose comedy-variety show became a lifeline for Austin’s gay community during the AIDS crisis; and Gilberto, a young Chicano activist whose camera documented both the gentrification of East Austin and the violence of an infamous 1983 Ku Klux Klan march through the city. Through these rediscovered moments, we watch characters evolve alongside Austin itself, each reflecting the sweeping changes of technology, culture, and an era coming to an end.

films.name: Art21: Delcy Morelos
films.short_description: Artist Delcy Morelos uses earth, seeds, fabrics, and spices to create immersive experiences that foster recognition of and respect for the Earth as a living entity, urging each of us to find healing and harmony through a dialogue with the natural world.
films.description:
In an ancient Carthusian monastery in Seville, Spain, artist Delcy Morelos works barefoot, her hands filled with scented soil and straw. This documentary short follows the artist as she uses earth, seeds, fabrics, and spices to create immersive experiences that foster recognition of and respect for the Earth as a living entity.


Reflecting on her life and work, Morelos recalls her childhood connection to nature in Tierralta, Colombia, her early paintings that respond to the decades-long period of violence in Colombia, and the meanings within monumental earthworks she is known for today, urging each of us to find healing and harmony through a dialogue with the natural world.

films.name: In The Still Of Night
films.short_description: On the Day of the Dead, a 10-year-old kid anxiously awaits a visit from his grandfather from the afterlife to finally meet him. He has to confront the skepticism of his parents, who discover that memory transcends life and death.
films.description: On the Day of the Dead, a 10-year-old kid anxiously awaits a visit from his grandfather from the afterlife to finally meet him. He has to confront the skepticism of his parents, who discover that memory transcends life and death.

films.name: Fish Die with Mar
films.short_description: Mar sinks into a journey through her subconscious, where water and fish carry her toward memories that seemed forgotten. Connecting with her childhood, she confronts the fears and traumas her body has never forgotten.
films.description: Mar embarks on a journey into her unconscious, exploring memories from her childhood that she thought were forgotten. The images of the fish at the aquarium she used to visit with her father still haunt her, and she slowly realizes that her memory is fragmented. Between past and present, she confronts the violence she endured and seeks to understand the complexity of her relationship with her abuser. In this process, she traces the invisible scars the trauma left on her body, trying to understand what really happened to her.

films.name: The Last Day of All
films.short_description: Three friends reunite to develop a roll of film filled with memories, while they confess the feelings they kept hidden.
films.description: Before leaving the city, Aldo decides to reunite with two former school friends on his last day of summer vacation. Hugo and Mar join him on a trip with the goal of developing a roll of film that holds shared memories, forcing them to confront the unfamiliar people they have become. Along the way, Aldo finally reveals the feelings he had kept hidden upon reconnecting with Mar.

films.name: São Paulo, New York
films.short_description: As his visa nears expiration, an aspiring hip-hop producer must choose between chasing his dream in New York or returning to São Paulo and confronting the life he left behind.
films.description:
As Felipe's visa nears expiration, he faces an impossible choice: remain in New York and fight to build a life as an immigrant and aspiring hip-hop producer, or return to São Paulo and confront the family, friendships, and music he left

behind. Told across two parallel timelines, São Paulo, New York explores belonging, cultural identity, and the meaning of success through a young man caught between two cities and two versions of himself.

films.description: After growing up on a cow farm in Dooen, Victoria, Anthony Walsgott worked as a secondary school teacher before transitioning into the legal profession. However, the confronting realities of what he saw on the farm as a child never left his mind. In 2010, Anthony abandoned his normal life to start the Save a Cow Foundation, where he committed himself to saving as many cows as possible from the slaughterhouse and looking after them for the term of their natural lives. For many years, he exhaustively managed cows across as many as 12 different properties. Several years ago, he and his partner acquired a beautiful 120-acre property along Queensland's Mary River, which is now a sanctuary large enough to accommodate 90 cow residents who call it home.

films.name: Uncommitted
films.short_description: Uncommitted follows Arab and Muslim American organizers who transform grief over Gaza into a grassroots movement that galvanizes nearly a million protest votes during the 2024 Democratic presidential primaries. From Dearborn to the Democratic National Convention, the film chronicles an emerging political coalition as it discovers its collective power and tests the possibilities, and limits, of representation, dissent, and American democracy.
films.description:
Uncommitted follows Arab and Muslim American organizers Lexi Zeidan, Layla Elabed, and Abbas Alawieh as they transform grief over Gaza into an unprecedented grassroots political movement. Beginning in Dearborn, Michigan, their campaign galvanizes nearly a million protest votes during the 2024 Democratic presidential primaries, challenging party leaders to support a ceasefire and demonstrating that their communities’ votes must be earned rather than assumed.


The movement carries its demands to the Democratic National Convention in Chicago, where even a request for a Palestinian American speaker is ultimately rejected. With intimate vérité access, Uncommitted focuses not on Palestinian suffering itself, but on what communities do in response, building coalitions, exercising political leverage, and challenging the institutions that claim to represent them.


More than an election documentary, Uncommitted captures the emergence of a new political coalition and a movement whose impact continues to reshape conversations about Palestine, representation, and political power in America.

films.description: WOOD STREET follows a year in the life of Oakland’s largest unhoused encampment as its residents face an imminent eviction that threatens to dismantle their community. As notices appear and police move in, residents organize — building barricades, filing lawsuits, and protesting at City Hall to fight for their right to stay. Told through immersive verité, the film places viewers inside the encampment, capturing the urgency, resilience, and emotional toll of collective resistance. At its center are John and LaMonté, whose bond is tested as pressure mounts — LaMonté’s mental health deteriorates while John struggles to remain sober. When the eviction comes, the community is physically erased, but its spirit endures.

Anna spends a decade obsessively building a detailed 1/3-scale version of her friend's house after losing her. It’s just big enough for Anna to squeeze through the door. Inside lives a puppet of her friend Yo. When the pair met, Yo was 73 and Anna just 24. Over the decades, they form a deep bond. After Yo's death, Anna re-constructs a magical space where Yo's stories unfold, and their relationship continues.


The film juxtaposes intimate vérité of Yo's last year with Anna's creative interpretations of Yo's dramatic life stories. Born in Switzerland in 1924, Yo lived life on her own terms, defying expectations around sexuality, mothering, aging, and even death. As the film blurs memory, time and invention, it also reveals the power of artistic creation to channel -and share- grief and love.

With rare proximity and emotional clarity, baby/girls offers a powerful portrait of young women coming of age in a place where choice, faith, and generational traumas collide.

films.description: When heading to the oceanside, one might expect to see surfers, joggers, and sunbathers—but not this. Each Sunday, a quiet yet powerful ritual unfolds as worshippers in Tijuana and San Diego gather on opposite sides of the border wall. Through song, prayer, and fellowship shared across rusty steel bars, an unexpected act of unity, faith, and resistance comes to life.

films.name: PUPPY LOVE Tails of the City
films.short_description: Through the stories of four New York City dogs and their humans, PUPPY LOVE: Tails of the City explores how the joys and challenges of dog parenting can transform our lives, deepen our capacity for care, and create unexpected communities on both sides of the leash.
films.description:
PUPPY LOVE: Tails of the City is an intimate short documentary exploring the heartwarming, and at times challenging world of dog parenting in New York City. Through the stories of four dogs and their humans, the film reflects on universal themes of connection, healing, community, and the profound transformation that happens on both sides of the leash.


From the journey of rescue and adoption, to the patience required to care for a reactive dog, to the tenderness and grief of loving a senior companion, each story reveals a different dimension of the human-dog bond. Along the way, dogs create unexpected networks of support, in parks, on sidewalks, at adoption events, and online, helping strangers become friends and turning a vast city into a community.


Ultimately, PUPPY LOVE reminds us that rescue is about more than saving one dog. It is about nurturing a more compassionate world where every being can feel safe, seen, and valued.

films.name: Landscapes of Memory
films.short_description: LANDSCAPES OF MEMORY follows Leah Galant’s journey through Germany as she reckons with family trauma and the weight of historical memory of the Holocaust. Interwoven stories of a Holocaust-survivor descendant, a Nazi-descendant historian, exiled Palestinian artists, and her father’s ALS, reveal the uses and abuses of memory culture.
films.description:
When director Leah Galant left the U.S. for Berlin in 2021, she thought she was going on a traditional “third-generation return” to uncover her family’s Holocaust history. But, after being detained while filming a pro-Palestine demonstration, and charged with antisemitism, she quickly realized that confronting inherited trauma meant grappling with the present, not just the past.


From brass “Stolpersteine” (stumbling stones) marking former Jewish homes, to concrete slabs, reminders of the Nazi regime’s atrocities are built into the German landscape. Yet cracks appear in those memorials. The rise of far-right extremism both in the streets and at the ballot box raises urgent questions about what lessons, if any, have truly been learned. Holocaust memory is often rigidly policed, Palestine activism is equated with antisemitism, and Arab and Muslim communities are increasingly surveilled and silenced.


LANDSCAPES OF MEMORY is a documentary weaving personal essay, observational storytelling, and intimate character studies to explore the uses and abuses of Holocaust memory. Filmed in the years before and months after the seismic shift of October 7th, the film follows three main protagonists: a third-generation Holocaust survivor’s descendant, Eli, a third-generation Nazi descendant, Johannes, and a Palestinian artist, Michael, each trying to understand what memory means in the present.


This journey through memorials past, present and future follows director Leah Galant’s personal exploration of history, memory and trauma. As her father’s health, and his ability to speak and share family histories, deteriorates from ALS, she takes on new responsibilities to carry her family's story of their Holocaust survival. Through voice notes, as he increasingly relies on text-to-speech, the film interweaves intimate yet universal explorations on the burden of history, and what it means to learn from the past to shape the present.

films.description: Seized is a gripping, stranger-than-fiction investigative thriller that plunges audiences inside the troubling police raid on the Marion County Record. What begins as a shocking small-town incident quickly spirals into a national story, exposing how corruption, politics, and decades-long tensions turned a quaint Kansas community into a battleground over the First and Fourth Amendments. Equal parts hilarious and horrifying, the film unfolds in real time through police body-cam and surveillance footage, revealing the raid’s chaos, the remarkable pettiness that led up to them, and the devastating personal toll on the newsroom, including the tragic death of its 98-year-old co-owner.

films.name: Glorious Summer

films.description:
A sun-drenched Renaissance palace. Three women exist in an airy state of suspension, a liminal, responsibility-free bubble, where summer never ends. An enigmatic system fulfills all their needs - providing food, entertainment and a daily routine focused on wellness affirmations. There’s just one rule: they are forbidden to cross the surrounding wall.


Soon, cracks begin to appear in this idyllic picture: using a ‘touch language’ - as some things can't be said out loud, secretly practicing how to die, which is supposed to be their ticket to ‘another place’. Long-suppressed anger and a desperate need to escape emerge. Will the girls, raised in a state of perpetual immaturity, manage to break free from the boundaries enforced by the system?

films.name: When We Were Live
films.short_description: Told entirely through restored public access footage, When We Were Live revives the unforgettable characters who turned an Austin community TV station into a world-famous stage for self-expression.
films.description:
Long before YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram, public access was the original platform for unfiltered creativity and community connection — a precursor to today’s social media, where ordinary people could broadcast themselves to their community.


Made up almost entirely of restored public access footage shot by Austinites over the last 50 years, each clip is a standalone story that reveals the city’s spirit from a new point of view. Among the film’s many characters are Livia, a PhD student turned late-night host whose uncensored sex-and-relationships call-in show became a cult favorite; Carmen Banana, a jovial drag queen whose comedy-variety show became a lifeline for Austin’s gay community during the AIDS crisis; and Gilberto, a young Chicano activist whose camera documented both the gentrification of East Austin and the violence of an infamous 1983 Ku Klux Klan march through the city. Through these rediscovered moments, we watch characters evolve alongside Austin itself, each reflecting the sweeping changes of technology, culture, and an era coming to an end.

Meg Littleton, amateur harpist and professional teacher’s pet, lives with her aunt, uncle and perennially popular cousin, Penny. When Meg discovers a commemoration ceremony is being planned for the shooting that took place at her high school ten years ago, she knows she must contribute something.


After all, the shooting claimed the lives of three students, and one teacher— Meg’s mom. Meg decides to stage a full, musical reenactment of the event, and convinces Penny to star in the show. With her cast of high school misfits, Meg attempts to pull off this bizarre, tender, and unwieldy undertaking— while the adults, armed with denial, dogma, and rubber bullet guns, do everything they can to stop her.

As strange occurrences in the house escalate, Mallory is forced to see each of these relationships - and her jealousy itself - in an entirely new light.

Yolanda alone possesses the true Sea-Monkeys formula and she alone must free them, not only from their captors, but also from the stain of her husband’s tarnished legacy.

films.name: The Last Critic
films.short_description: Robert Christgau, The Dean of American Rock Critics, whose work has inspired and infuriated readers for sixty years—is still at it in his eighties, grading records, interrogating commas and listening to absolutely everything (except heavy metal).
films.description:
The Last Critic is the first documentary feature about Robert Christgau, a pioneer of music criticism. The self-proclaimed Dean of American Rock Critics, Christgau helped invent the form in 1967 while covering the Monterey Pop Festival for Esquire, then redefined the form in 1969 with his Consumer Guide at The Village Voice—letter-graded, capsule reviews, 18 thousand of them over more than 50 years, and continuing to this day at Substack, where Christgau has been a best selling author since 2019.


A contributor to Rolling Stone, Creem, Spin, and The New York Times, Christgau made his greatest impact at The Village Voice as both an editor and writer. In the ‘70s, when pop music was defined by Fleetwood Mac and Billy Joel (who disliked Christgau almost as much as Christgau disliked him), he championed not just the punk of CBGB, but the funk of George Clinton and the soul of Al Green. He helped start the careers of generation after generation of gifted writers, among them Greg Tate, Colson Whitehead, Ann Powers, Joe Levy, Chuck Eddy, Nelson George, and Eric Weisbard. Now in his eighties, Bob is still at it, writing with the same vigor, concision and craft. From Thelonius Monk to James Brown, from The Ramones to Sleater-Kinney, from Aretha Franklin to Olivia Rodrigo, from Second Avenue to Soweto, no writer has considered Pop music with the force and flair as Christgau.

The film, directed by Pablo Aragüés, features never seen before vintage video footage taken by Copeland, himself. The documentary explores Copeland's journey from his childhood in Beirut to his rise to fame with The Police and his subsequent work on films and film scores, including Francis Ford Coppola's "Rumble Fish" and Oliver Stone's "Wall Street" The film features Copeland's dynamic reflections on his life and career, set against the backdrop of his performance at a beloved festival in the south of Italy.

films.name: (re)Dedicated - The Historic Restoration of Wichita's Orpheum Theatre
films.short_description: Chronicling the history of Wichita’s Orpheum Theatre and the concerned citizens who fought to save this legendary venue for the next generation of Wichitans.
films.description:
Opened in 1922, Wichita's Orpheum Theatre stood as a symbol of Wichita's early growth. But after 50 years of legendary performances and famous movies, the atmospheric-style theatre closed its doors in 1976.


Concerned citizens were determined not to let the historic theatre be demolished and fought to save it. Four decades later, and 104 years after it opened, the dream of countless individuals was finally realized when the Orpheum underwent a complete interior restoration. Now the theatre stands ready to entertain the citizens of Wichita for another 100 years.

films.name: Flooding Kaw Nation: Submerged Cities, Desecrated Graves, and Kaw Lake
films.short_description: In the 1970s, the federal government flooded the Kaw town of Washunga, Oklahoma to build Kaw Lake, inundating not only the homes but also the cemetery. films.name: Rainbow Rider
films.short_description: Rainbow Rider follows Shelle Lichti, an outspoken lesbian truck driver hauling freight across the country in her eponymous and iconic rainbow semi-truck. With her chihuahua sidekick in tow, Shelle encounters the joys of the open road, grumpy dispatchers, and lots of middle fingers sent in her direction.
films.description:
Shelle Lichti, a long-haul trucker and an unapologetically lesbian woman, drives the “Rainbow Rider”—a towering 18-wheeler wrapped in a blast of rainbow colors that can be spotted from miles away. On the open road, that visibility is powerful—and dangerous. From slurs on the radio to tire-stabbings, sabotage, and gunfire, Shelle has seen what hate can do. But she also knows what visibility can spark.


Rainbow Rider traces Shelle’s journey through truck shows, Pride festivals, and long stretches of highway as she works to build a network of support for LGBTQ+ truckers who are often isolated and vulnerable. Through moments of warmth, humor, and grit—from banter in the rain at the Walcott Jamboree, to consoling coworkers on the phone, to meeting relatives unexpectedly—the film reveals her mission: to make life safer for the next queer driver who rolls into a truck stop alone.


As Shelle opens up about a painful childhood, the violence faced by friends in the industry, and the strain of constant vigilance, the film becomes a portrait of resilience. Her truck, once the target of hostility, grows into a beacon—sparking conversations, inspiring allies, and encouraging others to express their identities on their own rigs.


In a world where the road can be merciless, Rainbow Rider shows how one woman turns a semi-truck into a symbol of hope, defiance, and chosen family.

She feels like a failure in every aspect of her life, but she desperately wants to be accepted by this new family. It takes every ounce of courage for her to get to the front door. films.short_description: A sister burdened with loss and responsibility tries to maintain hope for her and her brother in a resort town where luxury and hardship collide.
films.description: Frieda, a ski lift operator in Vail, navigates the harsh realities of life in a wealthy mountain town. Caring for her neurodivergent brother Frankie after the sudden death of their mother, Frieda struggles with guilt, loneliness, and financial instability. An encounter with her estranged ex forces her to confront unresolved pain and the weight of her responsibilities.

films.name: The Last Critic
films.short_description: Robert Christgau, The Dean of American Rock Critics, whose work has inspired and infuriated readers for sixty years—is still at it in his eighties, grading records, interrogating commas and listening to absolutely everything (except heavy metal).
films.description:
The Last Critic is the first documentary feature about Robert Christgau, a pioneer of music criticism. The self-proclaimed Dean of American Rock Critics, Christgau helped invent the form in 1967 while covering the Monterey Pop Festival for Esquire, then redefined the form in 1969 with his Consumer Guide at The Village Voice—letter-graded, capsule reviews, 18 thousand of them over more than 50 years, and continuing to this day at Substack, where Christgau has been a best selling author since 2019.


A contributor to Rolling Stone, Creem, Spin, and The New York Times, Christgau made his greatest impact at The Village Voice as both an editor and writer. In the ‘70s, when pop music was defined by Fleetwood Mac and Billy Joel (who disliked Christgau almost as much as Christgau disliked him), he championed not just the punk of CBGB, but the funk of George Clinton and the soul of Al Green. He helped start the careers of generation after generation of gifted writers, among them Greg Tate, Colson Whitehead, Ann Powers, Joe Levy, Chuck Eddy, Nelson George, and Eric Weisbard. Now in his eighties, Bob is still at it, writing with the same vigor, concision and craft. From Thelonius Monk to James Brown, from The Ramones to Sleater-Kinney, from Aretha Franklin to Olivia Rodrigo, from Second Avenue to Soweto, no writer has considered Pop music with the force and flair as Christgau.

films.short_description: A woman trapped in an endless cycle between reality and imagination struggles to break free from the eternal return of existence.

films.short_description: DJ Corey Grand is jumped in the park and seeks out the Guardians of Cleveland to defeat the villain responsible.

films.short_description: As a singer begs an ex-lover not to leave him behind, a phone call blurs the line between the present and a fading memory.
films.description: A visually driven music video depicting a phone call to an ex-lover, where the song is sung as a plea to be taken back and not left behind, while the ex-lover exists only as a fading memory.

films.name: SAME AS U
films.short_description: SAME AS U is a surrealist film that depicts an identity in transition. A series of every day backdrops with objects turning into other objects playfully match-cutting from one shot to the other. These objects are shape-shifting in a faceless world.
films.description: The identity shape-shifts as we live. We are always evolving through our surroundings, our teachings, and our communities. SAME AS U is a surrealist film that depicts an identity in transition—a goodbye letter to New York City, and to the person I was there. Released on the day of the 2026 Chinese New Year 2026, the film reflects transformation: we transition, we shape-shift, and we continue forward as the person we are able to be in this moment. Exploring visual transitions and the way each frame connects to the next, the film acts as a visual metaphor.

films.short_description: Fort Scott Stories is a continuing conversation first crafted by Gordon Parks in his hometown in 1950 with his Life magazine photo essay. The filmmaker picks up the trail illustrating a deeply moving, compelling and intimate portrait of present-day Fort Scott.
films.description: Fort Scott Stories offers a compelling and intimate portrait of present-day Fort Scott—capturing the heartbeat, character, and vibrancy of a community rich in history, resilience, and diverse cultural experiences. Through the voices of residents spanning generations—from youth to elders, business owners to church members—the documentary weaves together authentic narratives that reflect both the ordinary and extraordinary moments of life in Fort Scott that reflects the city’s enduring spirit.

films.name: All American Girls
films.short_description: All American Girls explores inclusivity in U.S. historical narratives through the famed American Girl brand, which was brought to life by legendary entrepreneur, Pleasant Rowland.
films.description: All American Girls pulls back the curtain, revealing the inner world of American Girl; the wildly popular brand that shaped girlhood for generations from the '80s onward. Today, the brand is a cultural touchstone, triggering debates about social and political issues. American Girl was founded by Midwestern schoolteacher Pleasant Rowland, who is sharing her story for the first time after evading the spotlight for decades.

films.name: A Woman's Work
films.short_description: A young woman in rural Kentucky works as a coal miner to provide for her two younger sisters after losing her parents; her father, who was also a coal miner, to the opioid epidemic.
films.description: Jolene has taken up a job in the coal mines in rural Kentucky - a job her father did before he died. She has to remain in the closet due to the place where she lives - while nothing is illegal, it is still frowned upon - and she accepts that there are certain sides of herself that she must keep hidden. Jolene constantly sacrifices for others; her love has to be hidden from prejudiced eyes, she works as a coal miner in order to keep a roof over her family's head and food on the table, and it rests upon her shoulders to care for her younger sisters even though she’s still figuring out how to care for herself.

films.name: baby/girls
films.short_description: Set in America’s Heartland, baby/girls follows three teens living in a maternity home as they navigate pregnancy and early motherhood. The film offers an intimate, unfiltered look at girlhood and motherhood colliding in the American South.
films.description: Teen birth rates in America’s Heartland are among the highest in the nation. Filmed over two years with intimate verite access, baby/girls follows Olivia, Grace and Ariana as they give birth and attempt to break the cycle of poverty, addiction, and abuse that has marked their own childhoods. With rare proximity and emotional clarity, baby/girls offers a powerful portrait of young women coming of age in a place where choice, faith, and generational traumas collide.

films.short_description: When Hollywood legend Harrison Ford makes his annual trips to Wichita, KS, the town buzzes with local folklore known as “Harrison Sightings." films.short_description: A timid young woman follows her boyfriend on a creative retreat to coastal Maine, but soon becomes convinced that she’s being haunted by the ghost of his ex-lover and muse.
films.description: Mallory, plagued by fears of being unremarkable, joins her playwright boyfriend Sam on a retreat to coastal Maine. When Sam's past — in the form of his captivating ex-girlfriend, Louise — comes back to haunt them, Mallory grows increasingly suspicious. Is Mallory being insecure, or does Sam have something to hide? As strange occurrences in the house escalate, Mallory is forced to see each of these relationships - and her jealousy itself - in an entirely new light.

films.description:
DYAD poetically explores the resilience and fragility of the human form set against the stark beauty of California's Mojave Desert towns. Directed by Katherine Helen Fisher with choreography by Allysen Hooks, the film follows two female dancers in evocative cycles of collision and symbiosis. Cinematographer Sinziana Velicescu emphasizes the aesthetics of emptiness and the disappearing sustainability of the landscape through minimalist visuals, sparse architecture, and expansive barren terrains. Meticulous editing and immersive sound design by John Walter, combined with Astrid Sonne’s tightly driven track, Stuck in Pause, heighten the film's meditation on vulnerability and ephemerality. Through metaphors of mitosis, DYAD subtly reflects humanity’s impact on Earth's delicate ecosystems, offering a contemplative vision of connection and identity in the Anthropocene.


DYAD

Katherine Helen Fisher is a choreographer, curator, and Emmy-nominated director whose work merges performance and computational media. She is the founder of Hyperreal Labs and co-founder of Safety Third, producing projects for Hermès, Radiohead, and PBS. Her curatorial project Dancing the Algorithm—an exhibition of algorithmically scored art—premiered at Jacob’s Pillow in 2025, inaugurating the new Doris Duke Theater. Funded by the Doris Duke Charitable Foundation and featured in The New York Times and Forbes, the exhibition highlighted performance as a site of algorithmic mediation. Fisher is also a Visiting Professor at NYU Tisch.


Allysen Hooks holds a BFA from Juilliard and an MFA from Sarah Lawrence, where she studied under John Jasperse and Beth Gill. Her choreography has been presented at Barnard Movement Lab, Austin Dance Festival, Tangente (Montréal), and commissioned by Contemporary Dance Wyoming, Indiana University, and others. A principal member of GALLIM (2012–2022), she performed worldwide, became Creative Associate to Andrea Miller, and contributed to commissions with companies including English National Ballet, Martha Graham Dance Company, and Ballet Hispánico. She has also worked with Jodi Melnick, John Jasperse, John Heginbotham, and taught at Rutgers University.

We are offered the sensations of sanctuary, yet beneath these still waters are the forces of a riptide of memory, recognition, and unattainable recovery.

You will be taken on an aesthetic and kinaesthetic voyage to what might be a very tangible place on earth or the most hidden site within the mind. From dark underwater depths to soaring above the clouds of Sweden, our female protagonist explores what it means to be human.

Dr. Maria Salgado Llopis (she/ her) is an award winning creative and interdisciplinary academic based in London. Her creative work and scholarship are deeply entwined and merge choreographing thoughts, writing gestures, scrutinising archives, dancing ideas and filming movement. As a researcher, Maria's work sits at the intersection between cultural studies, performance and body studies. She has presented her research, lectured, and performed her work internationally. She graduated from The John Cranko School in Stuttgart and holds a Master's Degree and a PhD in dance. She is currently Senior Lecturer at Middlesex University London and a freelance creative.

films.description: Oh Happy Day! follows an 8-year-old boy named Chris as he tries desperately to get the attention of his crush, Jazmyn. After several failed attempts, he devises a plan to risk it all. But, the question remains, will it work or will it be another missed opportunity to impress the girl of his dreams?

films.name: The last wish
films.short_description: When an unsettling visitor disrupts her fragile new life, a 70-year-old widow is compelled to face her greatest fear, water, forcing her into a battle with both her past and her own mortality.
films.description:
After the death of her husband, 70-year-old Rosabella moves in with her daughter Ruth, along with her granddaughter Romy. Barely settled, she decides to confront her greatest fear: water. Closer to death than to life, and determined to leave this world without regrets, she embarks on a journey to reconcile with her past. After an initial attempt, she reaches a breaking point. However, one morning, an unexpected and unsettling visitor pushes her to face both the water and her inner demons. Will she succeed?


The Last Wish is a drama that explores post-traumatic stress, highlighting the power of breaking painful cycles from the past.

films.name: Cleo & Zion
films.short_description: While on a road trip to visit their estranged mother, two divided sisters realize they are more alike than different.
films.description: Cleo is self-destructive. Zion has a need for control. When a petty crime and a charged reunion with an ex throw their trip into chaos, Zion finally admits the truth - their mother is dying. Forced to confront their childhood, Cleo and Zion realize all roads will always lead back to each other.

films.name: The Baltimore Barber
films.short_description: A beloved West Baltimore barber mentors a hopeful teen while the same violence that haunts his neighborhood begins closing in on them both.
films.description:
Anthony Evers is the best barber in West Baltimore, a trusted mentor whose shop is a sanctuary where clippers hum and young men share their dreams. Seventeen-year-old Scooter is one of his favorites, speaking excitedly about building a future for himself and his family as Anthony offers fatherly guidance.


Intercut with these moments is a colder ritual: Anthony working late at night, performing the same precise motions under very different circumstances.

films.description: Karina and Courtney share a strained silence over lunch. Courtney questions Karina about the state of her mental health journey. Karina says she is fine. Courtney doesn't believe her and pushes. Karina reacts in a way that changes the course of their friendship forever.

films.name: We're All Black Down Here
films.short_description: In a racially divided 1950s Britain, a black miner struggles to find acceptance above ground.
films.description:
In 1950s Britain, the coal mine is such a dangerous place that they have to look out for one another. Yet above ground, out of the showers when the coal dust is washed off, his fellow white miners treat Morris as an outsider. Emigrating from the Caribbean, Morris patiently endures subtle acts of racism, whilst seeking to fit in and gain acceptance.

In his situation when pushed to his limits Morris learns something about himself, and that to be accepted means also to accept.

films.name: The Peril at Pincer Point
films.short_description: On a quest to prove his competency, an inept sound recordist finds himself entangled in a nautical prophecy on the spectral island of Pincer Point.
films.description:
Jim Baitte, a layabout sound designer desperate to prove himself, is working on a new horror flick from the tyrannical yet lauded b-movie director P.W. Griffin. Accused of lacking vision and creative courage, Jim is sent to the remote island where the film was shot to capture a sound powerful enough to elevate the film's finale.


Once there, eerie local fables surface: for years, ambitious and headstrong youth have lost their souls to a ghostly sea captain for his spectral crew. As Jim entangles himself further into the bizarre locals, scenery, and prophecy, he can’t help but ponder the ever-confirming legend, and if recording it might just cost him more than his career.

films.name: Crystal Cross
films.short_description: A quirky Christian singer and a suicidal dad drive cross-country, forging an unlikely bond through bad decisions, bizarre roadside attractions, and an all-original soundtrack. "Crystal Cross" is a hilarious, bittersweet road trip about two lost souls finding comfort (but not salvation) in each other’s messes.
films.description:
Crystal Cross is the story of two unlikely companions on a doomed but beautiful road trip across America. Dotty, a Christian singer in trouble, believes she’s received a sign from God when she meets James, a man who looks strikingly like Jesus. For Dotty, James is her ride out of town and a chance to reverse her fate. For James, however, the journey has a darker purpose. Broken by the loss of his daughter and after several failed suicide attempts, he is driving cross-country to California to finally end his life.


What follows is an odd-couple love story — not quite a romance, but a connection that grows out of desperation, humor, music, and the long miles between them. Dotty clings to her dreams of stardom while hiding a secret that could destroy them both. James, a father without a child and a musician who no longer plays, resists every effort to be saved. As they travel, their bond deepens in strange, contradictory ways: moments of beauty at roadside attractions, recording booths, desert blooms, and drunken spirals reveal both their flaws and their fragile hope.


Crystal Cross explores the absurdity and tenderness of survival, faith, and failure in modern America. It is both a darkly comic odyssey and a meditation on love in its rawest form — love that doesn’t fix or promise, but simply keeps you alive for one more mile.
